title: SLO-adaptive trigger profiles for cost & latency-aware canaries
creator: Amina Patel
description: Motivation: current canary/rollback rules are static thresholds (p99 latency > X ms, error rate > Y%) which produce noisy aborts for workloads with heavy token-cost variance and traffic bursts. We need a system of adaptive trigger profiles that combines multiple SLO signals (latency quantiles, error rate, tokens-per-request cost, throughput) into an interpretable score and adapts thresholds per-route and per-cohort. The goal is to reduce false-positive auto-rollbacks and enable cost-aware rollouts where a model variant may sacrifice some latency for significant token-cost savings.
acceptance_criteria: A composable trigger profile exists that ingests latency quantiles (p50/p90/p99), error rate, per-request token cost, and throughput and outputs a single normalized ‘health score’
Profiles can be parameterized per-route and per-cohort (e.g., premium vs free-tier customers) with stored defaults and overrides
Auto-rollback policies can use health score bands with hysteresis (cooldown and grace windows) to avoid flip-flopping
A tuning job can run weekly to suggest adjusted thresholds using historical traffic windows (24h, 7d) and compare against baseline model to propose updates

End-to-end tests validate behavior using synthetic traffic: (a) bursty tokens with unchanged correctness; (b) systematic latency regressions; (c) cost-saving model with small latency increase — verify policy favors expected action
Dashboard tiles and alerts are created for health score, component signals, and decision audits (why a rollback was triggered)
implementation_notes: Health score = weighted z-scores of normalized signals with optional per-signal weight overrides; default weights: latency_p99=0.35, error_rate=0.35, token_cost=0.2, throughput_drop=0.1
Statistical test: use bootstrap-based confidence intervals for p99 shifts and CUSUM for sustained drift detection; avoid single-window heuristics
Profile storage: add `canary_profiles` table keyed by route+environment+cohort and exposed in rollout API
Decision service: new lightweight evaluator runs alongside rollout-orchestrator and records decisions to audit log with feature flags to enable gradual rollout
Hysteresis: require health score breach for 3 consecutive 60s windows OR 2 consecutive 5m windows before auto-rollback; allow shorter windows for P0 customer cohorts
Auto-tune: offline job computes suggested weights and threshold bands by minimizing false-positive rollbacks on last 30 days using historical incidents as labels
rollout_plan: Step 1 (canary): enable profile evaluator in dry-run mode for 10% traffic for 48h; record decisions but do not actuate
Step 2 (analysis): run auto-tune job and a manual review by oncall+PM; refine weights if needed
Step 3 (soft-actuation): enable auto-rollback for non-critical routes (free-tier) with conservative thresholds and 1h cooldown
Step 4 (wider): expand to 50% routes and add premium cohorts with tuned thresholds; monitor for 7 days
Step 5 (full): flip default canary policy to health-score-based for all new rollouts and keep legacy thresholds as fallback
test_plan: Unit tests for health-score computation and weight overrides
Integration test: simulate traffic traces (grpc + streaming) with token-cost variance; assert no spurious rollback in dry-run
Chaos tests: inject latency/error bursts and verify rollback triggers as expected and audit logs contain rationale
Backtest: run auto-tune offline on last 90 days across 5 representative routes and compare ROC of rollback decisions vs static thresholds
